name: raw chicken breast
descriptions: Fresh, uncooked chicken breast from a farm pack — intended for cooking before eating.
Dangerous if consumed raw: may carry bacteria leading to severe food poisoning.
effects: Impossible to enjoy raw — causes immediate foodborne illness symptoms if eaten without cooking.
Intended to be cooked into roasted, grilled or stewed dishes.

name: raw beef steak
descriptions: A cut of uncooked beef for steaks or stews.
Edible only after proper cooking; raw consumption risks bacterial infection.
effects: Causes severe foodborne illness if eaten raw.
Great source of protein when cooked and used in hearty dishes.

name: raw pork chop
descriptions: Uncooked pork chop, ready to be seasoned and cooked.
Pork should be fully cooked to avoid parasites and bacteria.
effects: Eating raw pork can cause severe gastrointestinal illness.
When cooked thoroughly it becomes a fatty, filling meal component.

name: raw fish fillet
descriptions: Fresh fillet from a recently caught fish — intended for cooking or safe cured preparations.
Some fish are edible raw if properly handled (e.g., sushi-grade), but untreated fillets can be risky.
effects: If not handled or frozen properly, raw fish can cause parasitic or bacterial illness.
When prepared correctly it can become baked, pan-seared, or used in safe raw dishes.

name: raw egg
descriptions: Fresh egg still uncooked — commonly used in many recipes but can carry salmonella if consumed raw.
Suitable for baking and cooking; avoid eating raw unless pasteurized.
effects: May cause foodborne illness if eaten raw.
Bakes into cakes, binds mixtures, or fries into a protein-rich meal when cooked.

name: raw milk (unpasteurized)
descriptions: Unpasteurized milk straight from dairy; intended for pasteurization before consumption.
Contains beneficial nutrients but also carries risk of harmful bacteria.
effects: Unpasteurized milk can cause severe gastrointestinal infection if consumed raw.
Once pasteurized it can be used for drinking, baking, and making dairy products.

name: Raw whole chicken (fresh)
descriptions: A whole chicken, plucked and ungutted, packaged for butchering or roasting.
Intended to be cooked thoroughly; eating raw poultry carries a high risk of severe foodborne illness.
effects: Consuming raw poultry causes immediate severe nausea and likely food poisoning.
Should be cooked to a safe internal temperature before eating.

name: Raw pork shoulder (bone-in)
descriptions: A large cut of fresh pork shoulder, commonly used for slow roasting or pulled pork.
Raw pork can carry parasites and bacteria; it needs extended cooking.
effects: Eating raw pork may induce stomach cramps and foodborne illness.
Best prepared slow-cooked or smoked to break down connective tissue.

name: Raw ground beef (1 lb pack)
descriptions: Freshly ground beef in a 1 lb portion, ideal for burgers, meatballs, or sauces.
Ground meat has a higher risk of bacterial contamination and must be cooked thoroughly.
effects: Eating raw ground beef commonly causes foodborne illness and severe stomach upset.
Should be cooked until no pink remains and juices run clear.

name: Raw ground pork (1 lb pack)
descriptions: Freshly ground pork, ready to be seasoned and used in sausages, meatballs, or stir-fries.
As raw ground pork, it should be fully cooked before consumption.
effects: Consuming raw ground pork risks parasitic infection and bacterial gastroenteritis.
Proper cooking eliminates most risks.

name: Fresh fish fillet (uncertified)
descriptions: A fillet of white fish caught recently and packaged for home preparation.
Not labeled as sushi- or sashimi-grade; may contain parasites or bacteria if eaten raw.
effects: Eating uncertified raw fish can cause foodborne illness or parasitic infection.
Recommended to cook thoroughly or use fish labeled sushi-grade for raw dishes.

name: Sushi-grade salmon fillet
descriptions: A carefully handled and frozen salmon fillet labeled sushi-grade, safe for raw preparations when handled correctly.
Suitable for sashimi, nigiri, or cured preparations if kept chilled.
effects: Eating sushi-grade salmon provides a clean, rich taste and a satisfying meal.
Provides quick energy and a healthy portion of protein and fats when eaten raw as intended.

name: Raw shrimp (shell-on)
descriptions: Fresh shrimp still in the shell, intended for peeling and cooking in a variety of dishes.
Raw shrimp can cause gastroenteritis if not properly handled or cooked.
effects: Eating raw shrimp can trigger stomach upset and foodborne illness.
Should be cooked until opaque and firm.

name: Fresh uncooked sausage links (pork bratwurst)
descriptions: A coil of fresh, uncooked pork sausage links that require thorough cooking before eating.
Typically seasoned and stuffed into casings but sold raw.
effects: Raw sausage contains fresh meat and should not be eaten without cooking; it can cause severe foodborne illness.
Best grilled, pan-fried, or simmered slowly until fully cooked.

name: Cured salami (ready-to-eat)
descriptions: A dry-cured salami, sliced and ready to eat. Curing and drying make it shelf-stable and safe without cooking.
Ideal for charcuterie boards, sandwiches, or snacking.
effects: Ready-to-eat cured salami can be eaten straight from the package and provides quick calories.
High in savory fat and salt; satisfying but dense.

name: Smoked kielbasa (fully cooked)
descriptions: A smoked, fully cooked kielbasa sausage that can be eaten cold or warmed.
Convenient as a ready-to-eat protein or for reheating in dishes.
effects: Provides immediate energy and satiety when eaten cold or after a quick reheat.
Hearty, smoky flavor suitable for stews, sandwiches, or as a snack.

name: Uncooked cured bacon (sliced)
descriptions: Thin slices of cured and partially smoked bacon sold raw; typically cooked before eating.
Although cured, raw bacon can still present some risk and is generally recommended to be cooked.
effects: Eating uncooked bacon may cause mild to moderate stomach upset for some individuals.
Best pan-fried or baked until crisp for safety and flavor.
